chunks: And from him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahbub, from Jamil ibn Salih, from Bukayr ibn A'yan, who said:
I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about a man who sends his zakat, and it is stolen or lost, so he said: 'There is nothing upon him (i.e., he is not liable to pay again).'
And that which indicates that when the recipient exists, he is liable (if it is lost), is what he narrated:
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on zakat if the money is stolen or lost before reaching the recipient?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that the obligation of zakat is discharged upon dispatch, meaning if the funds are lost in transit through no fault of the payer, they are exempt from re-payment. This ruling underscores the principle of 'ease' in Islamic jurisprudence, distinguishing between mere loss and liability due to negligence or custody, a key distinction in Shia fiqh regarding financial trusts. It highlights the reliability of the chain of transmission through the prominent narrators of the Tusi school, reinforcing the authenticity of this practical legal ruling.
